[
  {"quote": "Let's take a look at how it works.", "problem": "Informal, conversational filler. Technical documentation should state information directly."},
  {"quote": "It is designed to make incidents easier to route.", "problem": "Vague, promotional claim that says nothing concrete about what the feature does. The hedge \"designed to\" weakens it further."},
  {"quote": "Rules are robust and run in order.", "problem": "\"Robust\" is a vague marketing adjective that doesn't describe any behavior. The sentence should state the concrete property."},
  {"quote": "It's important to note that", "problem": "Filler phrase that adds no information. The sentence can state the point directly."},
  {"quote": "e.g. a deployment ID", "problem": "\"e.g.\" is an abbreviation for an informal aside. Use \"for example\" and set it off properly with punctuation."},
  {"quote": "You click **New Rule**.", "problem": "Procedure step is written in the second-person descriptive form. Numbered steps should use imperative verbs, as in the other steps (\"Click **Save**.\")."},
  {"quote": "The rule takes effect in 5–10 minutes.", "problem": "A statement about system behavior is embedded in a UI action step, which mixes procedure with explanation. It also gives a timing range without saying what determines it."},
  {"quote": "By following these steps, you can leverage your existing tags to seamlessly enrich every alert.", "problem": "Wordy and promotional. \"Leverage\" and \"seamlessly\" are jargon and fluff, and \"every alert\" overstates what the rules do."},
  {"quote": "*Rules are evaluated top to bottom.*", "problem": "Repeats the earlier \"run in order\" point. The italic styling is an inconsistent callout format, and the note is placed after the procedure, where it's easy to miss."},
  {"quote": "--max-time 5-10", "problem": "Invalid value in the code example. \"5-10\" is not a valid number for the timeout flag, so the example would fail if copied."},
  {"quote": "Read-only users can view rules but cannot edit them.", "problem": "Permission information is placed after the code block, separated from the related Admin permissions statement earlier in the document."}
]

[
  {"quote": "It is designed to make incidents easier to route.", "problem": "Vague, hedged purpose statement that says what the feature is meant for without explaining what it does."},
  {"quote": "Let's take a look at how it works.", "problem": "Conversational signpost that adds no information and doesn't suit reference documentation."},
  {"quote": "Rules are robust and run in order.", "problem": "\"Robust\" is an unsupported, promotional claim. The sentence should state the evaluation behavior plainly."},
  {"quote": "It's important to note that", "problem": "Filler phrase. State the point directly."},
  {"quote": "The Harness integration also sends tags", "problem": "\"Harness integration\" is not introduced or linked, so readers may not know what it is."},
  {"quote": "e.g.", "problem": "Latin abbreviation in running text. Use \"for example\" in documentation."},
  {"quote": "You click **New Rule**.", "problem": "Tense and mood are inconsistent with the other steps, which use imperative verbs (\"Open\", \"Enter\", \"Click\")."},
  {"quote": "Enter a tag name and a match condition.", "problem": "Incomplete instruction: the step doesn't say what value or tag the rule adds, even though the introduction says rules add new tags."},
  {"quote": "The rule takes effect in 5–10 minutes.", "problem": "Placed in step 3, before the Save step, so it reads as if the rule takes effect before it is saved. The timing is also a vague range with no stated cause."},
  {"quote": "leverage your existing tags to seamlessly enrich every alert", "problem": "Buzzwords (\"leverage\", \"seamlessly\") and wordy closing that adds no concrete information."},
  {"quote": "Rules are evaluated top to bottom.", "problem": "Repeats the earlier \"run in order\" point, and it is set in italics after the procedure, where it reads as an afterthought."},
  {"quote": "curl -X GET https://api.example.com/v2.1/enrichments", "problem": "The code block has no lead-in sentence, and it lists enrichments rather than creating a rule, so its purpose is unclear."},
  {"quote": "--max-time 5-10", "problem": "Invalid curl argument. --max-time takes a single number of seconds, not a range."},
  {"quote": "Read-only users can view rules but cannot edit them.", "problem": "Permission information is split from the earlier Admin requirement and placed after the code block, so it is hard to find."},
  {"quote": "— owner, service, and region —", "problem": "Paired em dashes make the sentence harder to parse. Parentheses or a shorter sentence would read more cleanly."}
]

[
  {"quote": "It is designed to make incidents easier to route.", "problem": "Vague, promotional claim that doesn't say what the feature does or how it helps routing."},
  {"quote": "Let's take a look at how it works.", "problem": "Conversational filler and a first-person-plural voice that doesn't belong in reference documentation."},
  {"quote": "Rules are robust and run in order.", "problem": "\"Robust\" is an unsupported, vague marketing adjective. The sentence also repeats the point made later in \"Rules are evaluated top to bottom.\""},
  {"quote": "It's important to note that", "problem": "Filler phrase that adds nothing; state the fact directly."},
  {"quote": "e.g. a deployment ID", "problem": "\"e.g.\" is an abbreviation that reads awkwardly in running prose; use \"for example\" or \"such as.\""},
  {"quote": "You click **New Rule**.", "problem": "Step is written in the present tense, while the other steps use imperative mood, so the list is inconsistent."},
  {"quote": "Enter a tag name and a match condition. The rule takes effect in 5–10 minutes.", "problem": "Step combines an instruction with a timing note. The timing belongs in a separate note or after the procedure."},
  {"quote": "By following these steps, you can leverage your existing tags to seamlessly enrich every alert.", "problem": "Wordy, buzzword-heavy closing (\"leverage,\" \"seamlessly\"). \"Every alert\" also overstates the scope, since rules apply to new alerts only."},
  {"quote": "*Rules are evaluated top to bottom.*", "problem": "Standalone italic note placed after the procedure. It repeats the earlier \"run in order\" statement and is not integrated into the text."},
  {"quote": "--max-time 5-10", "problem": "\"5-10\" is not a valid value for curl's --max-time, which takes a single number of seconds. The example is inaccurate."},
  {"quote": "Read-only users can view rules but cannot edit them.", "problem": "Permission note is placed after the code example, separated from the earlier Admin permission statement, so the access requirements are scattered."}
]
